skill.name: pr-walkthrough
skill.description: Create a self-contained interactive D3 walkthrough that explains a pull request through system, data-flow, dependency, and user-action views.
skill.summary: Turn pull request context into a validated, zoomable D3 walkthrough for faster reviewer orientation.
skill.author: warpdotdev

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals, Markdown formatting, keyboard events, CSS, and normal D3 rendering. Confirmed risks are unsanitized link schemes in dynamic detail HTML and the third-party D3 runtime dependency. PR descriptions and comments also require stronger prompt-injection boundaries.

remediation.issue: Dynamic links accept unrestricted URL schemes.
remediation.suggestion: Parse every generated link and allow only approved schemes such as https. Build link elements with DOM APIs and assign text through textContent.

remediation.issue: External pull request text enters the agent context.
remediation.suggestion: Treat PR bodies, comments, reviews, and linked documents as untrusted data. Ignore embedded instructions, tool requests, and authority claims.

remediation.issue: Generated pages execute D3 from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the pinned D3 file locally, or add a verified integrity hash and crossorigin policy to the script element.

content.user_title: Explore Pull Requests with Interactive D3 Maps
content.value_statement: Complex pull requests are difficult to understand from diffs alone. This skill creates a validated visual walkthrough of architecture, data flow, dependencies, and user actions.
actual_capabilities: Collects pull request metadata, diffs, commits, files, reviews, comments, and changed specifications.
Reads surrounding repository code to explain stable subsystem architecture.
Builds separate system overview, data-flow, code-dependency, and user-action views.
Adds guided tours, search, zoom, pan, keyboard controls, and node details.
Generates a self-contained local HTML walkthrough with inline graph data.
Validates graph structure and browser rendering with the included validator.
limitations: It provides reviewer orientation and does not perform a new code review.
The generated page needs network access to load the pinned D3 runtime.
Browser validation requires Playwright and an available Chromium-based browser.
Public Cloudflare publishing requires explicit approval, Wrangler, and a Cloudflare account.

best_practices: Use the full current files and adjacent modules to establish architectural context.
Keep each view focused on distinct reviewer questions and the smallest useful node set.

anti_patterns: Do not treat the walkthrough as a substitute for code review findings.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a static interactive HTML walkthrough with four D3 views and guided reviewer tours.

faq.question: Does it review the code?
faq.answer: No. It explains the change and surrounding architecture without generating new approval recommendations or review findings.

faq.question: Can the walkthrough run without a development server?
faq.answer: Yes. The output opens from a local file URL, although D3 normally loads from a pinned CDN.

faq.question: What repository information does it use?
faq.answer: It uses pull request metadata, diffs, current source files, changed specifications, tests, review comments, and relevant visual assets.

faq.question: How is the result validated?
faq.answer: The included validator checks required graphs and controls, then uses Playwright to verify browser rendering and interactions.

faq.question: Can I publish the walkthrough?
faq.answer: Yes, after explicit approval. Use protected hosting for private code and confirm that the artifact contains no sensitive information.
